record.paper_title: On chromatic numbers of space-times: open problems
record.original_question: Let Rm,n be a pseudo-Euclidean space with quadratic form D(A, B) = (a1 − b1)^2 + ... + (am − bm)^2 − (am+1 − bm+1)^2 − ... − (am+n − bm+n)^2, temporal distance τ(A, B) = √D(A, B) when D(A, B) ≥ 0, and spatial distance ρ(A, B) = √(−D(A, B)) when D(A, B) ≤ 0. What are the corresponding chromatic numbers χτ(Rm,n) and χρ(Rm,n), and how do they relate to the Euclidean bounds χ(Rm) ≤ χτ(Rm,n) and χ(Rn) ≤ χρ(Rm,n)?

evidence.quote: Case of general pseudo-Euclidean spaces. What if we consider a general pseudo-Euclidean space Rm,n
• the temporal distance τ (A, B) = √D(A, B) which is defined when D(A.B) ≥ 0, and • the spatial distance ρ(A, B) = √−D(A, B), which is defined when D(A, B) ≤ 0.
Here also natural embeddings lead to χ(Rm) ≤ χτ (Rm,n) and χ(Rn) ≤ χρ(Rm,n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $m,n\ge 0$, let $\mathbb{R}^{m,n}$ denote the pseudo-Euclidean space, i.e., $\mathbb{R}^{m+n}$ equipped with the quadratic form
$$D(A,B) = \sum_{i=1}^{m}(a_i-b_i)^2 - \sum_{j=1}^{n}(a_{m+j}-b_{m+j})^2,$$
for points $A=(a_1,\dots,a_{m+n})$ and $B=(b_1,\dots,b_{m+n})$. Define the temporal distance $\tau(A,B)=\sqrt{D(A,B)}$ when $D(A,B)\ge 0$, and the spatial distance $\rho(A,B)=\sqrt{-D(A,B)}$ when $D(A,B)\le 0$. Define the temporal chromatic number $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ as the smallest number of colors needed to color all points of $\mathbb{R}^{m,n}$ so that no two points $A,B$ with $\tau(A,B)=1$ receive the same color, and analogously define the spatial chromatic number $\chi_\rho(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ with the relation $\rho(A,B)=1$. The natural coordinate embeddings give $\chi(\mathbb{R}^m)\le \chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ and $\chi(\mathbb{R}^n)\le \chi_\rho(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$, where $\chi(\mathbb{R}^k)$ is the usual Euclidean chromatic number with forbidden distance $1$.

Determine $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ and $\chi_\rho(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ for general $m,n\ge 1$, and clarify the precise relationship between these quantities and the Euclidean chromatic numbers $\chi(\mathbb{R}^m)$ and $\chi(\mathbb{R}^n)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface any results determining the chromatic numbers $\chi_\tau(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ or $\chi_\rho(\mathbb{R}^{m,n})$ of general pseudo-Euclidean spaces. Even the classical Euclidean case $\chi(\mathbb{R}^n)$ remains famously unsolved beyond a few low-dimensional bounds, so the more general pseudo-Euclidean version appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: On the Clique and the Chromatic Numbers of High-Dimensional Distance Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys results on Euclidean chromatic numbers; no determination for pseudo-Euclidean (m,n) spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Existing literature focuses on Euclidean and normed spaces; the pseudo-Euclidean case is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Constructing 5-chromatic unit distance graphs embedded in the Euclidean plane
status_evidence.snippet: Even the planar Euclidean chromatic number is only known to be between 5 and 7.
status_evidence.claim: Classical Euclidean chromatic numbers remain open, suggesting pseudo-Euclidean analogues are also open.
